quests.instruction: You spend the whole afternoon laughing and playing with your best friends. How do you feel?
quests.question: Joyful
quests.hint: A whole afternoon full of laughter with people you love feels like deep, bubbling happiness.
quests.explanation: A whole afternoon full of laughter with people you love fills you with deep, bubbling happiness.
quests.funFact: Laughing together is known to make happy feelings even stronger between friends!

quests.instruction: You are staying overnight somewhere new and keep picturing your own kitchen. How do you feel?
quests.question: Homesick
quests.hint: Missing small, familiar details of home can give you a quiet, longing feeling.
quests.explanation: Missing small, familiar details of home gives you a quiet, longing feeling.
quests.funFact: This longing feeling usually fades once a new place starts to feel a little more familiar.

quests.instruction: Everything seems to go wrong today, one thing right after another. How do you feel?
quests.question: Miserable
quests.hint: A whole string of bad moments piling up together can feel like a heavy, deep low.
quests.explanation: A whole string of bad moments piling up together can leave you with a heavy, deep, low feeling.
quests.funFact: Even the hardest days are just one day — tomorrow always brings a fresh new start.

quests.instruction: You are hungry before dinner and keep muttering complaints about everything. How do you feel?
quests.question: Grumpy
quests.hint: Being extra hungry can make small things feel much more annoying than usual.
quests.explanation: Being extra hungry can make small things feel much more annoying, giving you a grumbly mood.
quests.funFact: This hungry, grumbly feeling is common enough that many people have a nickname for it!

quests.instruction: You keep thinking about how much nicer your friend's new skateboard looks than yours. How do you feel?
quests.question: Envious
quests.hint: Comparing your own things to a friend's newer ones can give you a wistful, wanting feeling.
quests.explanation: Comparing your own things to a friend's newer ones gives you a wistful, wanting feeling.
quests.funFact: Asking to try a friend's new gear together is a fun way to enjoy it without needing your own copy!

quests.instruction: Your friend forgets to save you a seat like they promised, and you end up sitting alone. How do you feel?
quests.question: Disappointed
quests.hint: This feeling is about someone not following through on a promise, more precise than simply feeling alone.
quests.explanation: This is disappointed rather than lonely — the precise feeling here comes from a broken promise, not from missing company in general.
quests.funFact: Telling a friend gently how you felt can help this kind of mix-up happen less often.

quests.instruction: You realize you have been walking around with your sweater on inside out all day. How do you feel?
quests.question: Embarrassed
quests.hint: This is the warm-cheeked feeling after a small mistake others may have noticed, not the quiet feeling of meeting someone new.
quests.explanation: This is embarrassed rather than shy — embarrassed fits a small mistake others may have noticed, while shy usually comes from being somewhere new or unfamiliar.
quests.funFact: A quick laugh at yourself is a great way to shrink this warm, self-conscious feeling fast!

quests.instruction: You are waiting backstage for your turn in the talent show you signed up for weeks ago. How do you feel?
quests.question: Nervous
quests.hint: This is the fluttery feeling before something planned, not sudden fear.
quests.explanation: This is nervous rather than scared — this fluttery feeling comes from something you knew was coming and prepared for.
quests.funFact: Performers often say this exact feeling fades the moment they take their first step on stage!

quests.instruction: Your kite keeps crashing every single time you try to launch it, no matter what you change. How do you feel?
quests.question: Frustrated
quests.hint: This is the stuck feeling of the same setback repeating, not a hot feeling about unfairness.
quests.explanation: This is frustrated rather than angry — frustrated fits the same setback repeating again and again, with nothing unfair involved.
quests.funFact: A little more wind or a longer tail on the kite can sometimes solve this exact repeating problem!

quests.instruction: Your brother breaks a promise and eats the snack he said he was saving for you. How do you feel?
quests.question: Angry
quests.hint: This is the hot feeling of someone treating you unfairly, not a stuck, repeating struggle.
quests.explanation: This is angry rather than frustrated — angry fits someone treating you unfairly, while frustrated fits a repeating struggle instead.
quests.funFact: Calmly telling someone how their broken promise made you feel can help prevent it next time.

quests.instruction: A large dog you do not know suddenly rushes toward you barking loudly. How do you feel?
quests.question: Scared
quests.hint: This is a sudden, jumpy reaction to something happening right now, not a slow-building flutter.
quests.explanation: This is scared rather than nervous — scared is the body's sudden reaction to something happening right now that feels unsafe.
quests.funFact: Standing still and staying calm is often the safest way to respond if this happens!

quests.instruction: You are the new student sitting quietly at a lunch table full of kids you do not know yet. How do you feel?
quests.question: Shy
quests.hint: This is the quiet, unsure feeling of an unfamiliar group, not the warm feeling after a specific mistake.
quests.explanation: This is shy rather than embarrassed — shy fits sitting with an unfamiliar group, since no actual mistake has happened here.
quests.funFact: Asking one simple question is often the easiest way to turn this quiet feeling into a new friendship!

quests.instruction: You and your friends play your favorite game outside until the sun goes down, laughing the whole time. How do you feel?
quests.question: Joyful
quests.hint: A whole day of play and laughter with friends feels like deep, bubbling happiness.
quests.explanation: A whole day of play and laughter with friends fills you with deep, bubbling happiness.
quests.funFact: Days like this, full of play and laughter, often become some of your happiest memories!

quests.instruction: You are staying at your grandparents' house and miss your own room. How do you feel?
quests.question: Homesick
quests.hint: Missing your own familiar space, even somewhere fun, can give you a longing feeling.
quests.explanation: Missing your own familiar space, even somewhere fun, gives you a longing, quiet feeling.
quests.funFact: A quick video call with home can help this longing feeling feel much smaller.

quests.instruction: Your favorite trip gets cancelled and it rains for the rest of the week too. How do you feel?
quests.question: Miserable
quests.hint: Several disappointing things happening one after another can feel like a heavy, deep low.
quests.explanation: Several disappointing things happening one after another can leave you with a heavy, deep, low feeling.
quests.funFact: Talking about a string of bad luck with someone you trust can help this heavy feeling lighten.

quests.instruction: You wake up on the wrong side of the bed and snap at everyone all morning. How do you feel?
quests.question: Grumpy
quests.hint: Feeling crabby and short-tempered for no clear reason can make you want to grumble at everything.
quests.explanation: Feeling crabby and short-tempered for no clear reason gives you a grumbly, irritable mood.
quests.funFact: A little extra rest or a favorite breakfast can sometimes help turn a grumbly morning around!

quests.instruction: You keep glancing at your classmate's perfect handwriting on the wall display. How do you feel?
quests.question: Envious
quests.hint: Comparing your own skill to someone else's polished result can give you a wistful feeling.
quests.explanation: Comparing your own skill to someone else's polished result gives you a wistful, wanting feeling.
quests.funFact: Handwriting, like any skill, keeps improving the more you practice it!

quests.instruction: You finally reach the front of the line, only to find out the ride is closed for the day. How do you feel?
quests.question: Disappointed
quests.hint: This is the specific letdown of a long wait not paying off, not a stuck, repeated struggle.
quests.explanation: This is disappointed rather than frustrated — frustrated fits a problem you keep struggling with, while this is a one-time letdown after a long wait.
quests.funFact: Most rides that close for the day reopen again on your very next visit!

quests.instruction: You accidentally call your friend by the wrong name in front of the whole group. How do you feel?
quests.question: Embarrassed
quests.hint: This is the warm-cheeked feeling after a small slip-up others noticed, not the quiet feeling of a new situation.
quests.explanation: This is embarrassed rather than shy — embarrassed follows an actual small slip-up, while shy comes simply from an unfamiliar situation.
quests.funFact: A simple correction and a smile is usually all it takes to move past a small name slip-up!

quests.instruction: You are about to walk into a spelling bee you have practiced for all month. How do you feel?
quests.question: Nervous
quests.hint: This is a fluttery, excited-but-unsure feeling before something you prepared for, not true fear.
quests.explanation: This is nervous rather than scared — nervous is that fluttery feeling before something you prepared for, while scared is for real danger or fright.
quests.funFact: This fluttery feeling almost always fades within the first minute of starting!

quests.instruction: You keep trying the same math problem and getting a different wrong answer each time. How do you feel?
quests.question: Frustrated
quests.hint: This is the stuck feeling of trying again and again without success, not a hot, unfair feeling.
quests.explanation: This is frustrated rather than angry — frustrated is the stuck feeling of trying repeatedly without success, with no unfairness involved.
quests.funFact: Trying a totally different method is often the key to finally solving a stubborn problem!

quests.instruction: Someone cuts in front of you in line even though you got there first. How do you feel?
quests.question: Angry
quests.hint: This is the hot feeling of something unfair happening to you, not a stuck, repeating struggle.
quests.explanation: This is angry rather than frustrated — angry fits something unfair happening, while frustrated usually comes from a repeating struggle instead.
quests.funFact: Politely reminding someone about the line often solves this kind of unfair moment quickly.

quests.instruction: You hear a loud, sudden bang like a firework go off right outside your window. How do you feel?
quests.question: Scared
quests.hint: This is a jumpy, startled feeling from something sudden, not the slow flutter before a planned event.
quests.explanation: This is scared rather than nervous — scared is your body's sudden, jumpy reaction to something startling, while nervous builds slowly before something you know is coming.
quests.funFact: Your body can react to a sudden loud sound before your brain even finishes understanding it!

quests.instruction: You have to introduce yourself to a room full of people you have never met. How do you feel?
quests.question: Shy
quests.hint: This is the quiet, unsure feeling of being somewhere unfamiliar, not the warm feeling after a mistake.
quests.explanation: This is shy rather than embarrassed — shy fits being somewhere unfamiliar with new people, while embarrassed usually follows an actual small mistake.
quests.funFact: This quiet feeling often fades quickly after just one friendly conversation!

quests.instruction: You spend the whole day at a fair full of laughter, rides, and treats. How do you feel?
quests.question: Joyful
quests.hint: A whole day full of fun, treats, and laughter feels like deep, bubbling happiness.
quests.explanation: A whole day full of fun, treats, and laughter fills you with deep, bubbling happiness.
quests.funFact: Fairs are designed with rides, games, and treats all together to create a full day of happiness!

quests.instruction: You are far away at camp and keep wishing you could hear your family's voices. How do you feel?
quests.question: Homesick
quests.hint: Missing the sound of familiar voices while you are away can give you a longing feeling.
quests.explanation: Missing the sound of familiar voices while you are away gives you a longing, quiet feeling.
quests.funFact: Many camps schedule a regular call day just to help campers feel connected to home.

quests.instruction: It rains through your entire camping trip from the very first night. How do you feel?
quests.question: Miserable
quests.hint: A whole trip you were excited for being rained out from the very start can feel like a heavy, deep low.
quests.explanation: A whole trip you were excited for being rained out from the very start can leave you with a heavy, low feeling.
quests.funFact: Many campers say playing games inside a tent can still make a rainy trip memorable!

quests.instruction: Nothing about today's plans sounds fun and you keep grumbling about it. How do you feel?
quests.question: Grumpy
quests.hint: Dreading a day that does not sound fun at all can put you in a grumbly, complaining mood.
quests.explanation: Dreading a day that does not sound fun at all can put you in a grumbly, complaining mood.
quests.funFact: Finding one small fun thing to look forward to can sometimes turn a grumbly day around!

quests.instruction: You keep glancing over at your neighbor's brand new treehouse. How do you feel?
quests.question: Envious
quests.hint: Wanting something great that belongs to someone else can give you a wistful, wanting feeling.
quests.explanation: Wanting something great that belongs to someone else gives you a wistful, wanting feeling inside.
quests.funFact: Asking if you can visit and play in a treehouse is a fun way to enjoy it without needing your own!

quests.instruction: You expected to win first place after months of practice, but you placed second instead. How do you feel?
quests.question: Disappointed
quests.hint: Think about the exact feeling when something almost goes your way but falls just short of what you hoped.
quests.explanation: This is disappointed rather than simply sad — it is that precise letdown when something almost goes your way but falls just short of your hopes.
quests.funFact: Placing second after all that practice is still a big achievement, even with this letdown feeling!
